title: REPORT on the implementation of the common foreign and security policy – 2024 annual report
part_text: 50. Takes note of the result of the presidential and congressional elections in the United States; recalls that the transatlantic relationship remains one of the most important and strategic relationship for the EU and its Member States, which has been emphasised by the unity and strength of the partnership demonstrated following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine; underlines that a strong transatlantic relationship remains indispensable for the security of the partners on both sides of the Atlantic; calls on the Commission to foster closer ties with key partners in both the US and Canada in order to counter global challenges that affect our shared values, interests, security and prosperity; in this context reiterates its call for EU-US summits to be held on a regular basis to provide top-level impetus to the future cooperation; fully supports the deepening of cooperation in the framework of the EU-US transatlantic dialogue, such as through transatlantic parliamentary diplomacy; calls for stronger transatlantic cooperation on trade, on foreign and security policy and on combatting challenges caused by rapid technological changes and growing cyber threats; welcomes in that regard the work of the Transatlantic Trade and Technology Council; is concerned about the impacts on human rights, poverty reduction and humanitarian assistance following the announced major budget cuts to the US Agency for International Development (USAID) and calls on the Commission to explore options to support staff hitherto working for USAID-funded organisations in countries where their safety may be compromised; encourages, furthermore, the EU to explore funding possibilities for projects of particular relevance to EU interests and priorities;
